title: Account Priority Trigger & Roadmap Commitment Policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a quantitative, ops-friendly policy that maps customer escalations and top-account signals to concrete roadmap commitment lanes. This ticket delivers: (1) a trigger matrix (contract + usage + severity) that automatically raises a Top-Account Priority Flag, (2) commitment windows and SLAs for product responses (commit to roadmap, SLA for delivery window, or offer funded-engineering paths), (3) an operational playbook for PM/ENG/Sales to validate and steward commitments, and (4) templates for customer communications and CSM handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Trigger matrix documented and approved by Sales Ops and Legal
Automated flag fields defined for CRM and Roadmap intake (ARR, active SLO breaches, incident severity)
Commitment lanes and timeboxes agreed (Immediate, Next Release, Funded, Backlog with SLA)
Communication templates and CSM/AE handoff checklist published in Confluence
Sign-off from Product Leadership and VP Sales on policy and resourcing implications
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Chose quantitative triggers over purely manual "escalation by request" to reduce bias and speed routing. Key signals: ARR >= $250k, active incident with severity >= Sev2 in last 14 days, repeated feature regressions reported by top-10 customers.

2025-02-21: Trade-off: committing to calendar delivery windows vs. committing to 'priority resourcing' + visibility. Decided to offer a hybrid: explicit calendar commits for contract-level obligations and priority resourcing + estimated window for others.
2025-02-26: Decided not to change pricing model as part of this policy; funded engineering track remains separate sales negotiation (captures urgent scope + dedicated SLA).
2025-03-01: Approval from Legal on contract-trigger wording; removed language that implied mandatory roadmap inclusion without resource alignment.
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Sales Ops, Solutions Engineering, Support, and Engineering GTM. Captured current pain points and examples (three recent customer escalations). Action: Sales Ops to export historical escalations for scoring calibration.

2025-02-20: Draft trigger matrix v0.1 created: signals = {ARR, incident_severity, feature_outage_count, strategic_partner_flag}. Scoring weights proposed: ARR(40), Severity(30), Frequency(20), Strategic(10).
2025-02-24: Workshop with Marisol Gomez (Dir. of PM) and Ethan Park (Sales Ops) to validate thresholds. Adjusted ARR threshold from $500k -> $250k for early product-market customers.
2025-03-02: Communication templates (Customer: commitment letter; Internal: PM handoff ticket template) drafted. Figma mockups for the customer letter created (see links).
2025-03-05: Policy brief circulated to Execs for review. Requested input on resourcing caps for 'Immediate' lane; awaiting ENG capacity confirmation.
notes_and_risks: Risk: Over-flagging could overwhelm engineering; mitigation = hard caps per quarter and requirement for Sales to accept potential 'funded' option.
Risk: Perceived promise creep — must ensure legal-approved language and CSM scripts are used for all commitments.
Note: Will integrate with Console's rollout dashboards to show customer-facing commitments and delivery status.
next_steps: Sales Ops to deliver historical escalation export and sample customer list by 2025-03-10
Engineering to confirm quarterly capacity uplift options by 2025-03-14 (ENG owners: Priya Nair)
Finalize trigger weights and publish v1 of the policy on Confluence by 2025-03-21
Prepare a pilot run for 2 enterprise customers (selected by Sales) for April 2025 to validate end-to-end flow
communication_templates: Customer commitment letter (template) - includes scope, expected delivery window, escalation contact, and funded-options clause.
Internal PM->Eng handoff ticket template - includes acceptance criteria, business impact, expected SLO uplift, and cross-functional owners.
CSM/AE script - approved wording to set customer expectations and avoid promise creep.
